title: Capacity ebb/flow KPI slate & launch capacity model
content:
Purpose:
This is a working KPI slate and lightweight capacity model for staging + first-wave launch traffic (pilot -> 10k DAU). Focus: capture ebb/flow patterns (daily spikes, weekly weekends, promo bursts), translate to autoscaling and reserved capacity recommendations, and produce an actionable pre-launch checklist for infra/product teams.

Summary of approach (TL;DR):
- Track three horizon KPIs: steady-state QPS per 1k users, burst multiplier, cold-start penalty.
- Use 3 scenario bands: base (expected), stress (1.5x), shock (3x short burst).
- Map scenario outputs -> capacity levers: dedicated GPU pool, burst slots, routing fallback to smaller quantized model.

Sheet layout (columns to copy into a dashboard):
- Metric | Unit | Target (pre-launch) | Baseline (last 30d) | Current | Owner | Action if off | Escalation SLA
- Examples: steady-state QPS/1k users | qps | 12 | 10.8 | 11.2 | eng-serving-runtime | bump pool by 1 node | oncall-eng
- Burst headroom (%) | % | 120 | 105 | 110 | infra | enable burst config | infra-pager
- Median p95 latency (prompt->first-token) | ms | <200 | 180 | 195 | eng-sre | enable KV-cache short window | sre-oncall

Concurrency / autoscale knobs mapping:
- Continuous batch target size -> affects median cost/token. Recommend: start with conservative batch target (B=4) during pilot, migrate to B=8 after stable p95 < 250ms.
- Idle pool buffer: keep N_reserved = ceil(peak_qps*0.15) as hot pool for 10-minute spikes.
- Burst policy: allow 2x burst for 15 minutes with auto-throttle to quantized model variants when tail latency > 400ms.

Capacity scenarios (quick sim notes):
1) Base (prob 0.6): 10k DAU, conversion 3% -> 300 active qps window -> steady QPS/1k=30. Outcome: needs 6 GPU workers (model-large) with batching 8.
2) Stress (prob 0.3): promo week, 1.7x sustained for 2 hours -> require +2 reserved nodes or fallback route.
3) Shock (prob 0.1): viral event, 4x for 10–20 minutes -> absorb via burst slots + degrade to quantized-medium model with 2s extra latency.

Launch readiness checklist (capacity-focused) - quick-run version:
- [ ] Autoscaler policy reviewed and merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/211)
- [ ] Dedicated pool sizing validated with perf bench (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Burst policy playbook written + runbook attached to oncall rotation
- [ ] Fallback model artifacts pinned and smoke-tested (quantized-medium)
- [ ] Prefix KV cache TTL baseline set to 5m and tested under sustained traffic
- [ ] Observability: token-level cost dashboard + p95 latency alert created
- [ ] Traffic-split routing configured for canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%)

Decision heuristics (when to add/remove reserved capacity):
- Add +1 reserved node if observed peak > 90% of pool capacity for 3 consecutive 10-min buckets.
- Remove -1 reserved node if 72h moving avg peak < 50% and no scheduled promos.
- Promote burst-to-reserved if burst events occur >2x in a 7-day window.

Runbook snippets (short):
- "High tail latency" (p95>400ms): trigger routing to quantized-medium, alert infra->sre, scale burst pool +1, set a 30 min lookout.
- "Sustained high QPS" (>1.5x baseline for >1 hour): move to stress mode, open incident channel, evaluate dropping non-critical routes.

Open experiments / notes-to-self:
- Run 10k Monte Carlo sim runs with variable user-session length distribution (0-30s prompt mix) to get 95th percentile GPU slot requirement. Link sim repo in artifacts.
- Try smaller KV cache TTL (2m) for chat-heavy workflows — measure regression to p95 latency.
- Need perf bench for quantized-medium vs large for long-context prompts (2k tokens).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: promos with long-form inputs (increases token cost) -> Mitigate: routing policy by input token-length to quantized variants and pre-warm KV cache for known prefixes.
- Risk: throttling cascading to upstream client errors -> Mitigate: circuit-breaker with gradual 429-based backoff and client-facing messages.

Owner matrix (short):
- Capacity modeling + sim: Marcus Nguyen
- Autoscale policy + infra config: Diego Torres
- Observability dashboards & alerts: Asha Patel
- Launch ops coordinator: Elena Brooks

Next steps (this doc):
1) Ship a small spreadsheet with the columns above and import last-30d telemetry (ask observability for tokenized export).
2) Run baseline perf bench across model variants (deadline: 2025-10-10).
3) Review autoscaler PR and schedule a dry-run during low-traffic window.

Unresolved questions: 
- What is the acceptable cost uplift for keeping 15% hot buffer during pilot? (finance stg request in JIRA-OPS-4245)
- Can Dedicated burst be purchased with a short term contract for promo windows? (legal check needed)

Notes for reviewers: this is intentionally compact — it's the SLA/capacity-side slice of the broader launch readiness docs. If you're on product-ops, please check the metric targets and add any customer constraints (e.g., regulated-beta cities).

Change log (brief):
- 2025-09-28 created (initial hypotheses + columns)
- 2025-10-07 updated: added decision heuristics and runbook snippets

—— end of slate ——
